verdict.rationale: Turso documents an official MCP integration through which an agent can manage databases and run SQL (turso-docs-9, turso-docs-37). Separately, database tokens can be restricted by database, permission level and expiration, with table- and action-level fine-grained permissions (turso-docs-56, turso-docs-57, turso-docs-8), and branching and PITR provide recovery from destructive mistakes (turso-docs-41, turso-docs-42). The evidence does not show that the MCP tools themselves separate read-only from destructive operations, and the MCP setup explicitly involves no API token, so it is unclear whether the scoped permissions apply to it. Missing for 10: MCP tool-level read-only vs destructive separation, evidence that scoped tokens or permissions govern MCP sessions, and hands-on or independent corroboration of safe agent delegation.
